# EvalKit

> EvalKit is a local-first kit for authoring agent evals as code. Teams can version TypeScript eval definitions in Git, reuse fixtures and executable predicate judges, compare configured model settings, and inspect or deliberately share local result files. This site is a static guide, not a hosted evaluation service.

## Documentation

- [Manual overview](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/manual/): Entry point to separate Markdown chapters for setup, agents, fixtures, scoring, CLI, reports, and troubleshooting. [Markdown sources](https://github.com/leostera/evalkit/tree/main/www/src/content/docs/manual).
- [Get started](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/): A walkthrough for the included starter project. [Markdown source](https://github.com/leostera/evalkit/blob/main/www/src/content/docs/index.md).
- [Project structure and discovery](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/manual/project-structure/): IDs, suites, config, and automatic discovery.
- [Agents under test](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/manual/agents/): AUT adapter and event contract.
- [Fixtures](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/manual/fixtures/): Candidate and evaluator workspace inputs.
- [Scorers and evals](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/manual/scoring-and-evals/): Predicates and eval definitions.
- [CLI and matrices](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/manual/cli-and-matrices/): Selection, runs, sweeps, and safety limits.
- [Results and reports](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/manual/results/): Local manifests, scoring, artifacts, and CI gates.
- [Troubleshooting](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/manual/troubleshooting/): Common issues and current limitations.
- [Repository](https://github.com/leostera/evalkit): Source code, contracts, tests, and examples.
- [Single-package install and publishing](https://github.com/leostera/evalkit/tree/main/packages/evalkit): `@leostera/evalkit` includes the authoring API, CLI, and dashboard. GitHub Packages publication is manual and has not happened yet.
- [Starter example](https://github.com/leostera/evalkit/tree/main/examples/starter): Runnable local project with default-exported eval discovery, no registry or config.
- [Configured matrix example](https://github.com/leostera/evalkit/tree/main/examples/configured-matrix): Runnable project with an optional `evalkit.config.ts` and a provider-free parameter sweep.

## Implementation notes

- Start with `bun create github.com/leostera/evalkit` to copy the monorepo (Bun installs its dependencies); then enter `evalkit/examples/starter` to run the self-contained greeting eval.
- Authored suites, evals, agents, and matrices use human-readable lowercase kebab-case IDs; the CLI selects evals and suites by ID. Fixtures have no ID: their destinations are scoped to an eval's trial workspace. Only runs and trials have generated URIs.
- The local CLI discovers default-exported `evals/**/*.eval.ts`/`.js` by default. An optional `evalkit.config.js`/`.ts`/`.mjs` customizes discovery and execution; `src/registry.ts` is for an optional explicit registry or suite. A config takes precedence over that file unless it explicitly supplies a registry. Reports are saved under `_evalkit-results/`.
- Config can define a parameter matrix with `id`, axes, defaults, and execution safety limits. Matrices expand lazily; select by ID with `run-matrix <matrix-id> --eval <eval-id>` and inspect a plan with `--dry-run`. The agent adapter must consume `context.parameters` for a model axis to change the model.
- The Agent Under Test (AUT) is the system whose behavior the eval measures, not the scorer. An adapter starts a fresh session, receives user messages, and emits events for scorers to inspect. Today `user(...)`, inline and final `predicate(...)` / `judge(...)` rules, and observed `expectToolCall(...)` checkpoints execute. Judge rules require a distinct eval-level agent. The `evalkit new` standalone project scaffold exists in the CLI but public `bunx @leostera/evalkit new` use awaits the first package release. Remote Agents SDK transport and enforced timeout policies are not available.
- Eval definitions can be versioned in Git; reports are local files, not automatically versioned or shared. The starter ignores report directories in Git; review for sensitive data and commit selected summaries if a versioned outcome history is needed. Run completion is not the same as a scoring pass: consult the run summary's `failed` count for trial outcomes.
- The website is static Astro served as Cloudflare Workers Static Assets. It does not run evaluations or expose an evaluation API.
